\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{রেওয়াজ} (reoyāj)}{রেওয়াজ (reoyāj)}]{\bn{রেওয়াজ} (reoyāj) — a custom; a common practice}

\label{lesson:BN-C353-reoyaj}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for deprived, then the Bengali for to include.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{রেওয়াজ}}
\textbf{\bn{রেওয়াজ}} — \emph{reoyāj} — \textquotedblleft{}a custom; a common practice\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বিয়েতে} \bn{এই} \bn{রেওয়াজ} \bn{পুরনো।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{biyete ei reoyāj purôno.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This wedding custom is old.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{রেওয়াজ}} (\emph{reoyāj}) is Persian \emph{rivāj}, currency and so a custom in general use, usually traced to Arabic: what people commonly do.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reoyāj}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reoyāj}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{biyete ei reoyāj purôno.} — This wedding custom is old.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for deprived, then the Bengali for to include, then say \emph{reoyāj} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{রেওয়াজ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A custom; a common practice\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{রীতি} (rīti)}{রীতি (rīti)}]{\bn{রীতি} (rīti) — a convention; a way of doing things}

\label{lesson:BN-C353-riti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to include, then the Bengali for a common practice.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{রীতি}}
\textbf{\bn{রীতি}} — \emph{rīti} — \textquotedblleft{}a convention; a way of doing things\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{অতিথিকে} \bn{চা} \bn{দেওয়া} \bn{আমাদের} \bn{রীতি।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ôtithike chā deoyā āmāder rīti.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Offering tea to a guest is our custom.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{রীতি}} (\emph{rīti}) is Sanskrit \emph{rīti}, a course or way and so usage and custom (Monier-Williams). It is the accepted way of doing something.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rīti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rīti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôtithike chā deoyā āmāder rīti.} — Offering tea to a guest is our custom.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to include, then the Bengali for a common practice, then say \emph{rīti} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{রীতি} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A convention; a way of doing things\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সংস্কার} (sôngskār)}{সংস্কার (sôngskār)}]{\bn{সংস্কার} (sôngskār) — a reform}

\label{lesson:BN-C353-songskar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a common practice, then the Bengali for a convention.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সংস্কার}}
\textbf{\bn{সংস্কার}} — \emph{sôngskār} — \textquotedblleft{}a reform\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আইনের} \bn{সংস্কার} \bn{দরকার।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āiner sôngskār dôrkār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The law needs reform.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সংস্কার}} (\emph{sôngskār}) is Sanskrit \emph{saṃskāra}, putting together well, perfecting (Monier-Williams). The sense 'a reform', a remaking of laws or customs, is a modern one.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôngskār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôngskār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āiner sôngskār dôrkār.} — The law needs reform.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a common practice, then the Bengali for a convention, then say \emph{sôngskār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সংস্কার} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A reform\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{প্রচলিত} (prôchôlitô)}{প্রচলিত (prôchôlitô)}]{\bn{প্রচলিত} (prôchôlitô) — current; in common use}

\label{lesson:BN-C353-procholito}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a convention, then the Bengali for a reform.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{প্রচলিত}}
\textbf{\bn{প্রচলিত}} — \emph{prôchôlitô} — \textquotedblleft{}current; in common use\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{এই} \bn{শব্দটা} \bn{এখন} \bn{আর} \bn{প্রচলিত} \bn{নয়।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ei shôbdôṭā ekhôn ār prôchôlitô nôy.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This word is no longer in use.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{প্রচলিত}} (\emph{prôchôlitô}) is Sanskrit \emph{pracalita}, set going and so current or customary (Monier-Williams): what is in use now.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prôchôlitô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prôchôlitô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ei shôbdôṭā ekhôn ār prôchôlitô nôy.} — This word is no longer in use.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a convention, then the Bengali for a reform, then say \emph{prôchôlitô} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{মানা} (mānā)}{মানা (mānā)}]{\bn{মানা} (mānā) — to obey; to keep (a custom, a rule)}

\label{lesson:BN-C353-mana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a reform, then the Bengali for in common use.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{মানা}}
\textbf{\bn{মানা}} — \emph{mānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to obey; to keep (a custom, a rule)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমরা} \bn{আমাদের} \bn{পুরনো} \bn{রীতি} \bn{মানি।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmrā āmāder purôno rīti māni.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We keep our old customs.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{নিয়ম} \bn{মানলেন}, \emph{tini niyôm mānlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{মানা}} (\emph{mānā}) is a tadbhava of Sanskrit \emph{mányatē}, thinks or considers; CDIAL 9857 lists Bengali \emph{mānā} 'to consider, obey'. To hold a rule worth heeding is to obey it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmrā āmāder purôno rīti māni.} — We keep our old customs.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a reform, then the Bengali for in common use, then say \emph{mānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{মানা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To obey; to keep (a custom, a rule)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Standing for Office to Customs and Change}

\label{lesson:BN-R353-review-346-353}



\begin{quote}
Say the Bengali for a candidate and a president.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a candidate, a president, a voter, to resign, to take an oath
  \item a government department, a town council, a village council, to appoint, to issue an order
  \item public revenue, a budget, a treasury, to collect dues, to sanction
  \item to protest, a blockade, public opinion, a policy, population
  \item an ideal, moral values, tolerance, truthful, fair
  \item to revere, to neglect, disdain, esteem, to treat with regard
  \item discrimination, dignity, sympathy, deprived, to include
  \item a common practice, a convention, a reform, in common use, to obey
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A candidate? (\textbf{\bn{প্রার্থী}}, \emph{prārthī}.) A president? (\textbf{\bn{রাষ্ট্রপতি}}, \emph{rāshṭrôpôti}.) A voter? (\textbf{\bn{ভোটার}}, \emph{bhoṭār}.) To resign? (\textbf{\bn{পদত্যাগ} \bn{করা}}, \emph{pôdôtyāg kôrā}.) To take an oath? (\textbf{\bn{শপথ} \bn{নেওয়া}}, \emph{shôpôth neoyā}.) A government department? (\textbf{\bn{দপ্তর}}, \emph{dôptôr}.) A town council? (\textbf{\bn{পৌরসভা}}, \emph{pourôsôbhā}.) A village council? (\textbf{\bn{পঞ্চায়েত}}, \emph{pônchāyet}.) To appoint? (\textbf{\bn{নিয়োগ} \bn{করা}}, \emph{niyog kôrā}.) To issue an order? (\textbf{\bn{জারি} \bn{করা}}, \emph{jāri kôrā}.) Public revenue? (\textbf{\bn{রাজস্ব}}, \emph{rājôsvô}.) A budget? (\textbf{\bn{বাজেট}}, \emph{bājeṭ}.) A treasury? (\textbf{\bn{কোষাগার}}, \emph{koshāgār}.) To collect dues? (\textbf{\bn{আদায়} \bn{করা}}, \emph{ādāy kôrā}.) To sanction? (\textbf{\bn{মঞ্জুর} \bn{করা}}, \emph{mônjur kôrā}.) To protest? (\textbf{\bn{প্রতিবাদ} \bn{করা}}, \emph{prôtibād kôrā}.) A blockade? (\textbf{\bn{অবরোধ}}, \emph{ôbôrodh}.) Public opinion? (\textbf{\bn{জনমত}}, \emph{jônômôt}.) A policy? (\textbf{\bn{নীতি}}, \emph{nīti}.) Population? (\textbf{\bn{জনসংখ্যা}}, \emph{jônôsôngkhyā}.) An ideal? (\textbf{\bn{আদর্শ}}, \emph{ādôrshô}.) Moral values? (\textbf{\bn{মূল্যবোধ}}, \emph{mūlyôbodh}.) Tolerance? (\textbf{\bn{সহিষ্ণুতা}}, \emph{sôhishnutā}.) Truthful? (\textbf{\bn{সত্যবাদী}}, \emph{sôtyôbādī}.) Fair? (\textbf{\bn{ন্যায্য}}, \emph{næjyô}.) To revere? (\textbf{\bn{শ্রদ্ধা} \bn{করা}}, \emph{shrôddhā kôrā}.) To neglect? (\textbf{\bn{অবহেলা} \bn{করা}}, \emph{ôbôhelā kôrā}.) Disdain? (\textbf{\bn{অবজ্ঞা}}, \emph{ôbôgyā}.) Esteem? (\textbf{\bn{কদর}}, \emph{kôdôr}.) To treat with regard? (\textbf{\bn{খাতির} \bn{করা}}, \emph{khātir kôrā}.) Discrimination? (\textbf{\bn{বৈষম্য}}, \emph{boishômyô}.) Dignity? (\textbf{\bn{মর্যাদা}}, \emph{môrjādā}.) Sympathy? (\textbf{\bn{সহানুভূতি}}, \emph{sôhānubhūti}.) Deprived? (\textbf{\bn{বঞ্চিত}}, \emph{bônchitô}.) To include? (\textbf{\bn{অন্তর্ভুক্ত} \bn{করা}}, \emph{ôntôrbhuktô kôrā}.) A common practice? (\textbf{\bn{রেওয়াজ}}, \emph{reoyāj}.) A convention? (\textbf{\bn{রীতি}}, \emph{rīti}.) A reform? (\textbf{\bn{সংস্কার}}, \emph{sôngskār}.) In common use? (\textbf{\bn{প্রচলিত}}, \emph{prôchôlitô}.) To obey? (\textbf{\bn{মানা}}, \emph{mānā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
